newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI share portfolio shows loss.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI share portfolio shows loss.

text.p: Share investments of finance firm Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) have been badly hit in the six months to September 30, 1996, and could impact current year profits, analysts said on Wednesday.
They said ICICI's portfolio investments -- which recorded a profit of 2,010 million rupees in the fiscal ended March 31, 1996 -- had incurred a notional loss of 2,660 million in the first half.
K.V. Kamath, ICICI's managing director, told analysts at a meeting on Tuesday that he was likely to provide for any loss in the firm's accounts for the year ended March 31, 1997.
"If this loss continues until March 31, ICICI is likely to provide for it and that will erode profits," said Prabodh Agarwal, banking analyst at securities firm James Capel B&K.
ICICI's investments have underperformed Bombay's benchmark stocks index which fell around 3.8 percent during the six-month period.
Analysts said the finance firm's portfolio comprised mainly of second tier stocks which have seen a sharper fall.
"I'm surprised that he made the commitment. It would wipe out second half profits," said Sandeep Nanda, head of research at Natwest Markets.
ICICI said on Tuesday net profit rose slightly to 2,663.0 million rupees in the six months to September 30, from 2,647.0 million a year ago. The results met most market expectations.
Kamath and other ICICI officials who briefed analysts on first half results were not immediately available for comment.
S.R. Krishnan, banking analyst at Peregrine Capital, said assuming the loss was steady at 2,660 million the loss net of tax would amount to around 2,120 million in 1996/97.
"It is bound to hit sentiment in the stock," Krishnan said.
ICICI shares were trading one rupee or 1.6 percent higher at 65 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
